hook: Scientists placed 1,815 sensors on Kīlauea to reveal what lies beneath.

sections.voiceover: Scientists placed 1,815 sensors on Kīlauea to reveal what lies beneath.
sections.visual_cue: Wide aerial view of Kīlauea summit with animated sensor points appearing across the landscape.
sections.sfx_cue: Low frequency rumble building into a sharp seismic ping.
b_roll: Graphic of 1,815 sensor icons mapped on volcano terrain

sections.voiceover: How did the researchers process 192 million seismic waveforms to map the volcano's complex subsurface?
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of seismic sensor equipment followed by a map showing a 30km radius circle around the summit.
sections.sfx_cue: Rhythmic ticking sound simulating data collection.
b_roll: Close-up of deployed seismic sensor on volcanic rock
Animated map showing 30km radius around Kīlauea

sections.voiceover: But the team analyzed 192 million seismic waveforms, revealing a far more complex structure.
sections.visual_cue: Visual representation of complex wave patterns pulsing and merging into a 3D subsurface model.

sections.voiceover: This deep analysis uncovered two distinct magma storage reservoirs. One reservoir sits beneath the Halemaʻumaʻu crater. A second chamber hides beneath the south caldera of Kīlauea.
sections.visual_cue: Cross-section 3D model of the volcano showing two glowing magma pockets labeled Halemaʻumaʻu and South Caldera.
b_roll: Labels pointing to Halemaʻumaʻu and South Caldera

sections.voiceover: Study co-author Roger Denlinger confirms these two chambers hold the molten secrets beneath Kīlauea.
sections.visual_cue: Slow zoom out from the summit to reveal the full volcanic structure.
b_roll: Slow aerial pull-back from Kīlauea summit
